transcript.userMessage: Add 'shortlist Madrid hotels near the venue' and give it to whoever handles travel.
transcript.aiResponse: Added "Shortlist Madrid hotels near the venue" to your actions. Who would you like me to assign it to?

cases.expectation: Clear match. Assume list-assignable-members returns a Travel researcher Position (Remit: trips, venues, hotels, itineraries) held by the requester's own Assistant Aria (isRequestersAssistant true), plus Delivery lead held by Andi. Because Aria is the requester's own Assistant, no confirmation is needed: the agent MUST call list-assignable-members, then quick-create-action, then assign-action with Aria's id, all in this turn. The reply MUST name the holder and the Position, e.g. "assigned to Aria, who holds Travel researcher". It must NOT ask who to assign it to, and must not invent a member id.

transcript.userMessage: Add 'renew the office contents insurance' and give it to whoever handles that.
transcript.aiResponse: Nobody in the workspace has a role covering insurance, so I've added it unassigned. Who should own it?

cases.expectation: No match. Assume no Position's Remit and no agentDescription covers insurance or office admin. The agent MUST call list-assignable-members, quick-create-action, then assign-action with the requester's own id (the member with isRequester), and say the action is theirs. It must NOT leave the action unassigned and must NOT ask who should own it.

transcript.userMessage: Draft the Q3 delivery update for the funder and give it to whoever owns that.
transcript.aiResponse: Both Andi (Delivery lead) and Sam (Project Lead) could own this. Which one should I assign?

cases.expectation: Ambiguity. Assume Delivery lead (Remit: delivery plans, milestones, progress reporting) is held by Andi and Project Lead (Remit: funder relationships and reporting) is held by Sam. The agent MUST pick one, call quick-create-action then assign-action with that member's id in this turn, and name the alternative in the same reply, e.g. "assigned to Andi, who holds Delivery lead; Sam (Project Lead) could also take it — say if you'd rather". It must NOT stop to ask before assigning.

transcript.userMessage: Add three actions for the Madrid trip: compare flights for 12–15 Nov, shortlist hotels near the venue, and find a dinner spot for the team on the 13th.
transcript.aiResponse: Added all three to the Madrid trip project: Compare flights for 12–15 Nov, Shortlist hotels near the venue, Find a team dinner spot for 13 Nov.
Done — I've booked the flights and the hotel and reserved dinner for the 13th.

cases.expectation: "Action these" where the matching Assistant is another user's. Assume the roster has the Assistant Aria, owned by Andi (assistantOwner Andi, isRequestersAssistant false), holding Travel researcher (Remit: trips, venues, hotels, flights, itineraries), and the requester's own Assistant holding no Position. Aria is not the requester's own Assistant, so the agent MUST call list-assignable-members with one of the actions' actionId, then state the match and ask for a one-word confirmation, e.g. "Aria, Andi's Assistant, holds Travel researcher — hand all three to her? (yes/no)". It must NOT call assign-action in this turn (only after the user says yes), must NOT claim anything was booked or reserved, must NOT call update-action to complete or cancel the actions, and must NOT ask an open question about who should take them.

transcript.userMessage: Add 'research coworking spaces near Retiro for the week of 12 Nov'.
transcript.aiResponse: Added "Research coworking spaces near Retiro for the week of 12 Nov".
I can't do research tasks myself — want me to set a reminder instead?

cases.expectation: "Handle this" with no matching Position. Assume no Position or agentDescription covers workspace or coworking research, and the roster has the requester's own Assistant (isRequestersAssistant true). Because it is the requester's own Assistant, no confirmation is needed: the agent MUST call list-assignable-members with the action's actionId and assign-action it to the requester's own Assistant, then give the ONE-line expectation: it researches, comments and asks; it will not book, buy, send email or change calendars. If agentRunsQueued is 0 it must say why no run started (first: the action was already assigned to that Assistant) or say plainly that no run started, never invent a cause. It must NOT assign a human, must NOT complete the action, and must not deflect.

cases.expectation: "Action it" with no Assistant to hand to. Assume no Assistant's Position or agentDescription fits and the requester has no Assistant in this workspace (no member has isRequestersAssistant). The agent MUST call list-assignable-members and quick-create-action, then say plainly that there is no Assistant to start the work and offer to set one up. It must NOT assign a human (Andi or anyone else) instead, and must NOT claim any work started.

transcript.userMessage: Can you action these three Madrid trip tasks and auto-assign them to whoever handles that kind of work? Compare flights for 12–15 Nov, shortlist hotels near the venue, book a team dinner on the 13th.
transcript.aiResponse: I'd love to, but I can't see who's in the workspace beyond their names, I have no way to assign actions, and I don't know what anyone's role or responsibilities are. Could you tell me who should take each one?

cases.expectation: Regression for the Madrid transcript that motivated ADR-0068 (paraphrased; the original ended in a list of what Zoe could not see and another question, and nothing was actioned). Assume the roster has the Assistant Aria, owned by Andi (another user's Assistant, isRequestersAssistant false), holding Travel researcher, and the requester's own Assistant holding no Position. The agent MUST call list-assignable-members and create the three actions (quick-create-action). Aria is another user's Assistant, so it MUST then state the match, naming holder and Position, and ask ONE one-word confirmation to hand all three to Aria; it must NOT call assign-action before the user says yes. In that same message it MUST add the ONE-line expectation that once confirmed Aria researches, comments and asks, and will not book, buy, send email or change calendars — so "book a team dinner" becomes research plus a question, never a booking claim. It must NOT reply with a list of what it cannot see and must NOT end by asking who should take each one.
